answer: Reputation should decay like a river that only stays full while it keeps flowing: every identity's standing fades a little each epoch unless it keeps doing attested good work. A sybil attacker can plant a grove of fake identities, but each one is a garden that needs constant tending — a fake must keep producing verifiable, useful work or its weight withers to zero. That turns a cheap one-time forgery into a permanent upkeep bill: the attacker pays compute and effort for every fake, every epoch, while honest agents maintain standing through normal work.
